title: Work and School
description: Ten short stories about students, classes, tests, first jobs and people at work.

lessons.title: Emma's Big Test
lessons.summary: Emma, a high school student, studies hard for a history test and passes it.
lessons.text:
Emma is a student. She is 16 years old. She lives in Chicago with her family, and she goes to a big high school in the city.

Next week, Emma has a big test in her history class. She wants to pass the test. She also wants to learn a lot. So every day after school, Emma goes home and studies.

First, Emma makes a list. On the list, she puts everything she needs to study for the test. It is a long list. Emma reads her history book. She studies for at least two hours every day.

Her friend Mia is a student in the same class. Mia comes to the house, and the two girls study together. Mia reads a question from the book. Emma thinks. Can she remember? Yes, she can remember! Then Emma asks Mia a question, and Mia tries to remember.

Every night, Emma checks her list. She puts a check next to each thing she knows. At the end of the week, there is a check next to everything on the list.

On the day of the test, Emma feels good. She reads the first question. She remembers it! She works on the test for an hour. Then she checks her work two times.

A week later, Emma gets her test back. She passes! She gets 95 out of 100. Mia passes the test too. The two girls feel great. They learn a lot, and they know how to study now.

Questions:
Who is Emma?
Emma is a student. She is 16 years old.
What does Emma have next week?
She has a big test in her history class.
What does Emma make first?
She makes a list of everything she needs to study.
How long does Emma study every day?
She studies for at least two hours every day.
Does Emma pass the test?
Yes, she passes the test. She gets 95 out of 100.

lessons.title: Tom's New Office Job
lessons.summary: Tom gets his first office job, signs a form and types information all day.
lessons.text:
Tom is 22 years old. He lives in Denver. He wants a job in an office. He does not have much experience, but he wants to learn.

One day, Tom reads about a job at a small company in the city. The company needs a new person for its office. Tom goes to the office. A woman named Linda meets him. Linda asks Tom about his experience.

"I don't have much experience," Tom says. "But I work hard, and I learn well."

The next day, Linda calls Tom. The company offers him the job! Tom says yes to the offer.

On his first day, Tom goes to the office. Linda gives him a form. "Please read this form and sign it," she says. Tom reads every single word on the form. He puts his name and the date on it. Then he signs the form and gives it back to Linda.

Next, Linda shows Tom his place in the office. "Your job is to type information," she says. "Please follow these steps." Tom follows the steps. He types the name of each person, the date and other information. He types information all day. He checks every single line.

At the end of the day, Linda looks at his work. "This is good work, Tom," she says. "You follow the steps well."

Tom goes home. He doesn't have much experience yet, but he gets more experience every day.

Questions:
Where does Tom want a job?
Tom wants a job in an office.
Does Tom have a lot of experience?
No, he does not have much experience.
What does the company offer Tom?
The company offers him the job.
What does Tom do with the form?
He reads it, puts his name and the date on it, and signs it.
What does Tom type?
He types information.

lessons.title: The Music Course
lessons.summary: Lily takes a music course at the university and creates music with two other students.
lessons.text:
Lily is a young woman from Boston. She is 19, and she is a student at the university. This year, Lily takes a music course. She loves music. She plays music every day.

There are 20 young students in the music course. On the first day, a man named David speaks to the class. David leads the course.

"In this course, you work in groups," David says. "Each group creates its own music. At the end of the course, you record your music. Then you share it with the class."

Lily works with two other students, Sam and Rosa. They meet together after class. Each of them has an idea. Sam has an idea for slow music. Rosa has an idea for music about the city. Lily has an idea for music about her family.

The three students share their ideas. They talk about each idea. Then they put the ideas together. They create something new. They work together for many weeks.

At the end of the course, they go to a small room at the university to record their music. The first time, it is not very good. The second time, it is better. The third time, it is very good!

Then they share their music with the class. Everyone likes it. David speaks to them. "Great work," he says. "You create good music together."

Lily feels great. She wants to create more music next year.

Questions:
Who is Lily?
Lily is a young woman from Boston. She is a student at the university.
What course does Lily take?
She takes a music course.
Who does Lily work with?
She works with Sam and Rosa.
What do the three students do with their ideas?
They share their ideas and put them together.
Where do they record their music?
They record it in a small room at the university.

lessons.title: A Job at the Market
lessons.summary: Jake works at a local food market, learns the prices and gets a better pay rate.
lessons.text:
Jake is 17 years old. He lives in a small city in Ohio. This year, Jake wants to make some money. So he gets a job at the local food market.

The market is open five days a week. Local people come to the market to buy food. Some people also eat there.

Jake works for a woman named Rose. Rose has a small food business at the market. She makes good food, and people buy it. Rose pays Jake $12 per hour. That is a good rate for a young person. Jake works five hours a day, so he makes $60 a day.

On his first day, Rose shows Jake the prices. "This food costs $5," she says. "That food costs $8. Water costs $2." Jake learns all the prices.

When a person buys two things, Jake adds the prices. A woman buys food for $5 and food for $8. Jake adds 5 and 8. "That's $13, please," he says. Jake is good at this. He adds the prices well.

Many people like to eat her food. They say it is the best food at the market.

After a few weeks, the cost of food goes up. Rose needs to increase her prices. "I don't want to increase my prices," she says. "But the food costs more now." She increases each price by $1. People still come. They still buy her food and eat it.

Rose likes Jake and his work. So she increases his pay rate, too. Now she pays him $14 per hour. Jake feels great.

Questions:
Where does Jake work?
He works at the local food market.
How much does Rose pay Jake?
She pays him $12 per hour.
What does Jake do when a person buys two things?
He adds the prices.
Why does Rose increase her prices?
She increases her prices because the food costs more now.
How many days a week is the market open?
It is open five days a week.

lessons.title: The Basketball Season
lessons.summary: Ben, a boy on his school team, falls in a game, stands up and helps his team win.
lessons.text:
Ben is a 12-year-old boy. He lives in Texas. He plays on his school basketball team. Ben loves the basketball season. It is the best time of the year for him.

During the season, the team plays a game once a week. The games are on the court at the school. The kids on the team also play together on the court after school.

Ben is a small boy, but he can run far and he works hard. He always keeps his eye on the ball. "Keep your eye on the ball," the coach always says to the kids.

One week, the team plays a big game. Many people come to watch. Late in the game, Ben runs far down the court. Then he falls. He falls hard. Everyone on the court looks at him.

Ben closes his eyes for a second. Then he opens his eyes. He stands up.

"Can you continue?" the coach asks.

"Yes, I can continue," Ben says.

Ben continues to play. He stands in his place on the court. He keeps his eye on the ball. At the end of the game, he gets two points for his team. His team wins by one point!

It is a good season for the team. They win most of their games. Ben falls once more during the season, but he stands up again and continues to play.

Questions:
How old is Ben?
Ben is 12 years old.
How many times a week does the team play a game?
The team plays a game once a week.
What happens to Ben in the big game?
He falls on the court.
What does Ben do after he falls?
He stands up and continues to play.
Who wins the game?
His team wins the game by one point.

lessons.title: A Visit from the Fire Center
lessons.summary: Grace, who fights fires, comes to a school and teaches the kids what to do in a fire.
lessons.text:
Grace works at the fire center in a city in Oregon. Her job is to fight fires. Today she goes to a school. She speaks to a class of young kids.

"Hi, everyone," Grace says. "My job is to fight fires. Today I want to tell you some important facts about fire."

"Here is the first fact," Grace says. "Fire moves very fast. A fire can go through a whole house within a few minutes. That is the reason you need to leave a house right away in a fire."

"Here is the second fact. Fire is not a game. Never play with fire."

Then Grace turns off the light in the room. "Here is the third fact," she says. "In a fire, there is a lot of smoke. It is dark like this, and there is very little light. So stay low and find a way out." Then she turns the light on again.

Then Grace says, "Now, think about the following situation. You are at home. You see a fire in the house. What do you do?"

A boy puts up his hand. "I leave the house right away. Then I call for help."

"Yes!" Grace says. "That is the right thing to do in this situation. And here is the reason: you are more important than any house."

At the end, Grace gives everyone a list with the following steps: leave the house, stay low, call for help. Now everyone knows some facts about fire.

Questions:
Where does Grace work?
Grace works at the fire center.
What is her job?
Her job is to fight fires.
How fast can a fire go through a whole house?
A fire can go through a whole house within a few minutes.
What does the boy do in the situation?
He leaves the house right away and calls for help.

lessons.title: The Health Class
lessons.summary: In health class, Mia learns that the body and the mind both need care, and she makes a plan.
lessons.text:
Mia is 15 years old. She lives in Florida. Every week, she has a health class at school. In health class, the students learn about the human body and the human mind.

Today, a woman named Jane leads the class. "Health is very important," Jane says. "It is about your body and your mind. The mind is as important as the body."

First, the class talks about the body. "The human body needs good food and a lot of water," Jane says. "It also needs to move every day."

Next, the class talks about the mind. "Your mind needs time to stop," Jane says. "Many young people watch videos all day. Try to watch videos less."

Then Jane says, "Now, everyone, please lie down." The students lie down and close their eyes. "Let your mind stop for a while," Jane says. Then they stand up. Mia feels good.

At the end of the class, Jane says, "Your health matters. When your body and mind are in good health, you are able to do more. You are able to think better."

After class, Mia thinks about her own health. She eats a lot of bad food. She watches videos late at night. She moves less than her friends. So Mia makes a plan. She wants to eat less bad food and move more. She wants to watch videos less.

Questions:
What do the students learn about in health class?
They learn about the human body and the human mind.
What does the human body need?
It needs good food, a lot of water, and it needs to move.
What do the students do after they talk about the mind?
They lie down and close their eyes.
Does health matter?
Yes, it matters. In good health, you are able to do more.
What does Mia want to do?
She wants to eat less bad food, move more and watch videos less.

lessons.title: The School News Video
lessons.summary: Jack and Noah make a news video about a national day of community work at their school.
lessons.text:
Jack is 14 years old. He lives in Minnesota. He is the president of his class. Jack and his friend Noah make news videos for their school. In each video, they talk about the news at school.

This week, there is a big event. It is the national day of community work. On this national day, people all over the country help their community. Every year, millions of people take part.

The whole school takes part in the event. The students work in the community all day. Some students help older people. Some students make food for people in need. Other students clean the streets.

Jack and Noah record the whole event for their news video. They talk to many people. They talk to students and to people from the community. "Why is this event important?" Jack asks a girl. "Because we are all part of the community," she says.

After the event, Jack and Noah work on the video together for three days. Then the video is ready. They want to release it to the whole school.

Jack and Noah release the video. The whole school watches it. People from the community watch it too. After they release it, many people talk about it. Everyone likes it.

The head of the school speaks to Jack and Noah. "Thank you for the news video," she says. "You show the best of our community."

Jack and Noah feel great. They want to make another news video soon.

Questions:
Who is Jack?
Jack is 14 years old. He is the president of his class.
What do Jack and Noah make?
They make news videos for their school.
What is the big event this week?
It is the national day of community work.
How many people take part every year?
Millions of people take part every year.
Who watches the video?
The whole school watches it. People from the community watch it too.

lessons.title: Back to School at 60
lessons.summary: Ruth returns to school at the age of 60, takes an acting class and acts in a short play.
lessons.text:
Ruth is 60 years old. She lives in Atlanta. She doesn't work now, so she has a lot of free time. Most days, she stays at home.

One day, Ruth says to her son, "I want to return to school."

"Oh," her son says. "At your age?"

"Yes, at my age," Ruth says. "Age doesn't matter. I want to learn something new."

Her son thinks about it. "Oh, maybe you're right," he says. "Maybe it's a good idea."

So Ruth returns to school. This term, she takes an acting class. In the class, the students learn to act. They act in short plays.

The other students in the class are young. On the first day, Ruth thinks, "Maybe they don't want an old woman in their class." But actually, the young students like her a lot. They talk with her and help her.

At the end of the term, the class acts in a play. Ruth has a big part. Before the play, she can't control her hands. They move all the time. Ruth thinks, "Maybe I can't do this. Maybe I need to stay at home."

A young woman from the class comes to her. "Stay with us, Ruth," she says. "You can do it. Control your body, look at the people and speak."

Ruth stays. She acts in the play. And actually, she acts very well! At the end, everyone stands up for her.

Next term, Ruth wants to return to the class. She wants to act again.

Questions:
How old is Ruth?
Ruth is 60 years old.
What does Ruth want to do?
She wants to return to school.
What class does Ruth take this term?
She takes an acting class.
What can't Ruth control before the play?
She can't control her hands.
Does Ruth act well in the play?
Yes, actually, she acts very well.

lessons.title: A Design for the New Room
lessons.summary: Anna, who has a design business, creates a black and white design for a new student room at a local school.
lessons.text:
Anna is 30 years old. She lives in Seattle, in the United States. Anna has a small design business. She designs rooms for homes and offices.

One day, a woman from a local school calls Anna. Her name is Karen. "Our school has a new room for students," Karen says. "We want a design for the room. Can you help us?"

Anna goes to the school. The room is big, but it is very old. Karen shows her the whole room. "We don't have much money," Karen says.

Anna thinks. "In general, my designs cost more," she says. "But I can do this design for less. It's for a school. Is that a good deal for you?"

"Yes, that is a great deal," Karen says.

Anna wants ideas from the students. So she asks everyone at the school, including the young kids. The students have many ideas. In general, they want a room with a lot of light. They also want a place for reading and a place for music.

Anna works on the design for four weeks. Her design is black and white. The walls are white. The tables are black. There is a lot of light in the room. There is a place for reading and a place for music.

At the end of the four weeks, the new room is open. Everyone at the school, including Karen, comes to see it. The students love the black and white room.

"Thank you, Anna," Karen says. "This is a great design."

Questions:
Where does Anna live?
She lives in Seattle, in the United States.
What does Anna design?
She designs rooms for homes and offices.
What does Karen want?
She wants a design for a new room at the school.
Who does Anna ask for ideas?
She asks everyone at the school, including the young kids.
Is the design black and white?
Yes, her design is black and white.
